opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that in such cases, it was believed to be the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. But she could not, for she had never desired his good opinion, and he had certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. She was sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone, but it had been most unconsciously done and she hoped it would be of short duration. opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that she might as well ask why, with such a clear intention of offending and insulting her, he chose to tell her that he liked her against his will, against his reason, and even against his character. Had not her own feelings decided against him, had they been indifferent, or even favourable, did he think that any consideration would tempt her to accept the man who had been the means of ruining, perhaps forever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?
